hypothesis: The integration of large language models (LLMs) with drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction systems can enhance the accuracy and efficiency of identifying binding affinities by leveraging advanced deep learning techniques. LLMs have demonstrated robust capabilities in processing and generating complex data structures, which can be applied to model protein sequences and drug compounds effectively [2406.19384]. The use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to model 1D representations of targets and drugs has already shown promising results in predicting binding affinities, outperforming traditional methods like KronRLS and SimBoost [1801.10193v2]. By incorporating LLMs, which excel in predictive processing and reasoning [2105646118], the prediction models can potentially improve their interpretability and generalization across diverse datasets [2501.12948]. Furthermore, LLMs can automate the extraction of interpretable features from complex datasets, enhancing the understanding of DTI mechanisms [F76bwRSLeK]. This approach aligns with the trend of using AI to automate and optimize scientific discovery processes [2409.05890].
